A bill prepared in the State Duma proposes special periods when cinemas would either stop screening foreign films or sharply limit their share of screen time, TASS reports.

The proposal also sets fees for distribution certificates: 5 million rubles for foreign live-action films and 3 million for animation.

It would require cinemas to allocate 10% of their quarterly box-office revenue to developing Russian films. Some of the funds would also support schedule monitoring to check compliance.

The bill envisions periods throughout the year when foreign films would be banned or heavily restricted.

The rules could take effect on March 1, 2027.
